findings.summary: The provider settings page and the per-project env editor SERVE the real saved credential VALUE in the HTTP response / DOM (confirmed: live GEMINI_API_KEY value in the raw HTML of GET /settings/providers).
findings.contract_conflict: browser-and-secrets.md:59 ('masked so the rendered image cannot contain a credential') and core-invariants.md:47 ('masked from logs, prompts, and artifacts') say the value must be ABSENT. The UI treats 'masked' as a password-input visual with a show/hide toggle, so the value IS present.
findings.codified_by_tests: test_ui_settings.py::test_settings_page_shows_the_stored_value_masked; test_ui_env_editor.py ('masked input carrying the value, with a show/hide toggle') -- the tests lock in the value-present behaviour, so the suite is green while the contract is violated.
findings.authorization: No DECISIONS.md entry authorizes weakening the credential boundary. Under the Lab Protocol, weakening a safety invariant needs an Approved-by D-entry first.
findings.decision_required: Umesh: (A) accept value-visible owner-only local editor -> a DECISIONS entry + amend browser-and-secrets.md / core-invariants.md to scope the boundary to non-UI artifacts and state the residual (value reaches HTTP responses, DOM, screenshots); or (B) bug -> restore F-026 never-echo (render empty inputs; the value never enters the response).
findings.note: Real value redacted everywhere. Local browser snapshot that captured it was deleted; .playwright-mcp is gitignored; .env (the value's correct home) is gitignored.

minor_notes: settings inputs emit 4 VERBOSE console hints ('inputs should have autocomplete=new-password') -- benign; adding autocomplete=new-password would silence them
verdict: 3/4 surfaces clean and interactive; 1 high-severity credential-boundary violation surfaced for a CRITICAL human decision. Read-only validation only -- no run triggered (Pathlynks/live runs are credential-gated).
